bull.b: Completion of the IgA nephropathy cohort advances vensobafusp alfa toward meaningful clinical readouts and supports dose-selection work in a defined renal indication. Expanding into focal segmental glomerulosclerosis also broadens the potential development opportunity across complement-mediated diseases with substantial unmet need.

The large PIPE materially strengthens near-term development capacity for a clinical-stage company without commercial revenue. Funding through the second half of 2028 gives Jasper more time to advance multiple programs, reach clinical milestones, and pursue value-creating regulatory or partnering outcomes.

The Kira transaction broadened Jasper’s portfolio beyond its original mast-cell focus and concentrated resources on immune-mediated and rare diseases. The out-licensing deal provides external validation and upfront capital while allowing another company to develop selected assets, preserving strategic focus.

bear.b: Jasper remains dependent on clinical development rather than recurring product sales, so operating performance cannot yet be supported by commercial revenue. Continued losses and the absence of operating leverage leave future financial progress highly dependent on successful trials, approvals, and eventual commercialization or partnering.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means Jasper must continue using its financial resources to fund research, trials, and corporate operations. Even with recent funding, ongoing burn can reduce flexibility over time and creates continuing dependence on capital markets, partnerships, or other financing sources.

The approved capital-structure tools provide financing flexibility but also indicate that Jasper may need to manage a very large share base while funding development. A higher authorized share count and potential reverse split can facilitate future equity issuance, creating dilution risk for existing holders as programs advance.
